text: Goldman's 1967 causal theory analyzes knowledge as requiring an appropriate causal connection between the fact that p and S's belief that p. Which objection identifies a class of knowledge the theory struggles to accommodate?
choices: It cannot explain perceptual knowledge, because perception involves no causal contact between object and believer.
It collapses into the no-false-lemmas view, since every causal chain must contain a false intermediate belief.
It entails that the truth-conditions of knowledge attributions shift with the attributor's conversational standards.
It cannot easily accommodate mathematical knowledge, since necessary truths do not stand in causal relations to beliefs.
explanation: Abstract, necessarily true propositions such as those of mathematics do not cause anything, so the causal theory struggles to explain how we know them; Goldman's appeal to causal processes of proof and instruction only attenuates the causal requirement. Perceptual knowledge (option 0) is in fact the theory's paradigm success case. Option 2 describes contextualism, a distinct semantic thesis about the word 'knows,' not an objection to the causal theory.
